title: Rollback Playbook Simulator with Human-in-the-Loop and Cost Impact Estimates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated rollback system that runs a simulated dry-run of config changes (batching/caching/quantization) and surfaces a human-in-the-loop approval when economic or quality risks exceed configurable thresholds. The system should provide: (1) a cost-oriented simulator that estimates per-token unit cost delta, (2) staged validation windows (dry-run, shadow, canary, ramp), (3) deterministic state snapshots and idempotent apply/rollback primitives, and (4) a reconciliation loop to detect divergence between desired and actual runtime state and perform safe backfills or corrective rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator produces per-change cost delta estimate within ±10% of measured cost in shadow runs
Rollback trigger fires automatically when at least one high-severity condition is met and will produce an auditable event with the reason and delta estimate
Human-in-the-loop approval path exists for changes that exceed configured cost/quality thresholds and records approver and rationale
State reconciliation loop can detect and correct stale KV cache states or failed partial applies within 10 minutes for 95% of simulated failure modes
Integration tests cover dry-run → shadow → canary → rollback transition and pass in CI against a mocked runtime
design_notes: We treat config change rollout as a 4-stage pipeline: dry-run (simulator only), shadow (traffic mirrored, no serve), canary (small cohort), ramp (full rollout). Each stage has independent metrics windows and rollback thresholds.

Simulator uses historical token distribution and per-model kernel profiles to estimate cost impact for batching/kv-cache/quantization changes. We keep a lightweight ML model (XGBoost) to predict cost delta from features: average seq len, cache-hit-rate, batch-size distribution.

We will snapshot runtime state (applied config + KV cache map + routing version) before each staged apply. Snapshots are stored in S3 with versioned keys and an integrity hash to allow deterministic rollback.

Human-in-the-loop flow must support timed auto-approve for low-risk changes (P3 by default) and require explicit approval for high-impact changes. Approval metadata must be stored in the audit log and surfaced in Console.
We will provide a simulator API endpoint and a Console UI card showing: estimated cost delta, quality risk score, expected latency impact, and recommended staging plan.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype simulator using historical traces and implement dry-run API; store snapshots and basic audit events
Week 2: Implement shadowing infrastructure and telemetry hooks to measure real cost and quality in mirrored runs
Week 3: Add canary orchestration with per-cohort thresholds and automatic rollback executor; integrate human-approve gating in Console
Week 4: Build reconciliation daemon that compares desired state vs observed state and kicks corrective actions; add automated backfill for cache warming
Week 5: End-to-end testing, security review, and rollout to staging; iterate on thresholds based on simulation results
rollback_triggers: Cost spike: sustained >20% increase in per-token cost across canary cohort for 5 minutes
Latency regression: p95 latency increase >400ms over baseline for 3 consecutive windows
Error rate: 0.5% absolute increase in 500-series errors or timeouts
Output divergence: automated eval set quality drop >8% (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-distance heuristics) compared to baseline
Telemetry de-synchronization: KV cache hit-rate drops >30% vs shadow expectation indicating cache corruption or mismatch
guardrails_and_controls: Require signature-approved change for any config that simulator tags as 'high cost risk' (estimated delta >15%)
Max-canary-size cap default 1% of traffic for high-risk changes; configurable per-team
Quarantine mode for affected KV cache keys: mark keys as read-only and trigger async repopulation after rollback
Safe-apply primitive is idempotent and requires precondition checks (observed hash matches expected) before committing
Circuit breaker to pause rollout if upstream capacity or GPU availability drops below reserve threshold
reconciliation_flow: Monitor loop compares stored desired_state(snapshot_id) vs reported_node_states every 30s
If mismatch detected, run a simulated dry-apply using the snapshot in a sandbox and validate side-effects
If sandbox simulation passes, execute auto-repair: re-apply config with backoff and warm KV cache using prioritized prefixes
If sandbox simulation fails or indicates cost/quality risk, trigger rollback and notify owners
All reconciliation actions produce deterministic audit records and optional automated PR that documents change+reconciliation steps
testing_and_simulation_results: Initial dry-run simulations on historical traffic (last 30 days) show predicted cost delta MAE 9.2% against measured shadow runs
Shadow run for batching strategy B-3 reduced per-token cost by ~12% for long-tail sequences but increased p95 latency by 70ms in heavy concurrency tests
Simulator flagged 3 changes as high-risk that manual inspection confirmed would blow up KV cache hit-rate due to stale prefix assumptions
Chaos test: simulated partial apply + node failure reliably triggered reconciliation loop and produced correct snapshot-based rollback in 98/100 runs
rollout_plan: Stage: internal dev cluster (dry-run, no traffic) — Week of 2025-02-24
Stage: staging with mirrored traffic (shadow) — Week of 2025-03-03
Stage: canary 0.5% traffic with auto-rollback triggers enabled — Week of 2025-03-10
Stage: ramp to 10% then progressively with cost/quality gating — target full rollout by 2025-03-29
Fallback: manual rollback runbook ready and on-call rotation notified during canary windows
